related_resources.reason: Excavations of five Classic-period residential terraces document construction episodes, maguey fiber work, stone tools, household variation and small differences in nonlocal goods.
Reports mapping and survey of El Palmillo, Guirún and Mitla Fortress and regional household-craft research in the Oaxaca valley.
Six excavated residential terraces: some craft activities widespread at different intensities, others limited to some households; differential but modest exotic-material access.
Measurements of spindle whorls from eight residences suggest several fiber types and households with different production mixes; whorls do not preserve complete textiles.
Supplementary orientation only, not used to substantiate historical claims.
